transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been having a hard time stopping my worrying once it starts. It can be about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work. Even if I make lists or try to redirect myself, I just can’t seem to put it away in my mind.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get very worried and uncomfortable, but I can’t say it comes on suddenly and peaks within a few minutes like that.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
I’m not really sure. I know I worry a lot, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether I feel physically restless or on edge.
Do you often feel tense in your muscles?

Yes. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel really tight, almost locked up. I think I’m bracing myself without realizing it. I also catch myself clenching my jaw when I’m answering emails or listening for my mother in the next room.
Have you ever had a period of intense fear or discomfort that seemed to come out of the blue?
Not really, no. I get uncomfortable and worried, but I wouldn’t say it comes out of nowhere like that.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your worrying?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I avoid things in a clear, deliberate way because of worry. I may put things off sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed avoiding specific situations or activities.
Is your worrying usually focused on a specific issue or does it seem to be about a wide range of things?

It’s a wide range of things now. It used to be mostly about my mother’s safety, but over the past year it’s spread—money, decisions at work, deadlines, the house, whether I’m being a good daughter. Even small things can start to feel like they’re going to unravel.
Do you think your worrying is excessive or out of proportion to the actual situations you're worrying about?

Yes, I think so. In the moment it feels reasonable, but when I step back, it does seem bigger than the situation calls for. Like, this past year it’s gone from just worrying about my mother’s safety to worrying about finances, work decisions, deadlines, the house, whether I’m being a good daughter… and even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of fear or anxiety that was overwhelming?
I don’t think so. I get very anxious and worked up, but I wouldn’t say it comes on suddenly like an overwhelming wave of fear. It’s more like worrying builds up.
Do you find that your worrying is present most of the time?

Yes, most of the time lately. It’s not always the exact same worry, but it keeps shifting—my mother’s safety, money, work decisions, deadlines, the house, whether I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.
Has your worrying been interfering with your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

Yes, it has. At work I’ve started missing small but important details at the library, which really isn’t like me. And I froze during part of a grant presentation and had to hand pieces of it off to someone else. That shook me up, honestly, because I’m supposed to be leading the team, and now I worry whether I’m doing that well enough.
Do you usually feel tense in your muscles when you're worrying?

Yes. By the end of the day my neck and shoulders feel really tight, like I’ve been bracing myself all day. I also notice I’m clenching my jaw when I’m answering emails, or even just sitting there listening for my mother in the next room.
How much distress do you feel when you're worrying?

It’s pretty distressing. Not every minute is unbearable, but when it gets going, it can feel hard to settle down or think clearly. I’d say it’s enough that I notice it affecting my day, and I feel worn out by it.
Do you often feel like you're fidgeting or have an inability to sit still when you're worrying?
I’m not sure I’d say I can’t sit still. I haven’t really noticed a lot of fidgeting. I might shift around a bit when I’m anxious, but it’s not one of the main things I notice.
Do you feel like you can control your worrying when it starts?

Not really. Once a worry starts, it’s hard for me to put it away. It can be about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or wondering if I missed something at work, and even if I make lists or try to redirect myself, it just keeps going in my head.
Do you feel restless when you are worrying?
I don’t really know. I wouldn’t say restlessness is a big part of it for me. I might feel keyed up inside, but I’m not usually pacing around or feeling like I have to move.
